findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:53,112,137,165 — async legacy writes derive their context from the incoming request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)); net/http cancels the request context when the handler returns, so the background Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls nearly always run against an already-canceled context and fail, silently diverging legacy from unified storage on every write. The parent must be context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or background), not the request ctx; tests pass only because they use context.Background().

[High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:136-143 (Update) — the updateWrapper that pinned the legacy write to the exact object persisted by Storage was removed; Legacy.Update now re-invokes objInfo.UpdatedObject against legacy's own 'old' object, so the two stores can persist different contents (different resourceVersion/defaults, or a divergent result if the update function isn't idempotent), breaking write-equivalence between stores.

[High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:103-107 (Delete) — early return on any storage error, including NotFound, skips the legacy delete entirely; the previous code tolerated apierrors.IsNotFound and still deleted from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy (pre-migration) can now never be cleaned up, leaving permanent orphaned legacy rows.

[Medium/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:156-160 (DeleteCollection) — when the unified-store DeleteCollection fails, the legacy DeleteCollection is never attempted (previously it always ran), leaving orphaned legacy objects on partial failures.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:47 (Create) and :131 (Update) — on storage failure the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration, so storage errors are recorded as legacy-store failures and no storage-failure metric is emitted, breaking error monitoring for the primary store.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:168 (DeleteCollection goroutine) — the legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded via recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency/errors to unified-storage metrics.

[Medium/performance] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:108 (Delete) — the success path passes the user-controlled object name where the kind label belongs (d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)) while the error path uses options.Kind; per-object-name labels cause unbounded Prometheus cardinality (users can blow up the metrics with many distinct names) and inconsistent label values.

[Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:52-59,110-116,136-143,163-169 — all four async legacy writes swallow errors: the result is only reflected as a boolean in a metric with no log.Error (the previous code logged legacy failures); callers get success even when the legacy write later fails, so store divergence leaves no log trail and there is no retry/reconciliation.

[Medium/performance] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — every Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine with no queue, concurrency cap, or backpressure; under write load against a slow legacy store, thousands of concurrent legacy operations (each holding up to a 10s timeout) can pile up and exhaust the DB connection pool shared with the primary store.

[Low/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:99 (Delete) — ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) injects the base logger instead of the enriched log built on line 98, so context-scoped log lines from this path lose the name/kind/method fields (all sibling methods inject log).

[Low/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — the spawned goroutines have no panic recovery; a panic inside a legacy storage implementation (or in the metric recording) on a bare goroutine crashes the entire apiserver process.

[Low/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — async legacy writes are untracked (no WaitGroup/shutdown coordination), so writes in flight during process shutdown/restart are silently dropped with no retry, producing gaps in legacy data.

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — tests never assert the defining behavior of mode 3: that writes are dual-written to legacy (no assertion that LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection were invoked, no AssertExpectations); because legacy writes are async, the goroutine can invoke the mock after the subtest returns (racy/flaky), and every test uses context.Background(), which is exactly why the canceled-request-context defect goes undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Critical/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:53,112,137,165 — async legacy writes derive their context from the incoming request context (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)); net/http cancels the request context when the handler returns, so the background Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls nearly always run against an already-canceled context and fail, silently diverging legacy from unified storage on every write. The parent must be context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (or background), not the request ctx; tests pass only because they use context.Background().

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes are moved into goroutines (Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection) and each goroutine derives its context from the passed-in ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). Since these methods return immediately after the unified Storage operation, if ctx is a request-scoped net/http context it will typically be canceled when the handler finishes, causing the async legacy calls to run with an already-canceled context and fail. The diff shows no use of context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background() for the goroutines. The new tests invoke these methods with context.Background(), so they would not catch this cancellation behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:136-143 (Update) — the updateWrapper that pinned the legacy write to the exact object persisted by Storage was removed; Legacy.Update now re-invokes objInfo.UpdatedObject against legacy's own 'old' object, so the two stores can persist different contents (different resourceVersion/defaults, or a divergent result if the update function isn't idempotent), breaking write-equivalence between stores.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous Mode3 Update flow that computed `updated := objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old)` from Storage's current object and then used an `updateWrapper` to ensure both Storage and Legacy saw the same updated object. In the new implementation, `d.Storage.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` is called directly and then `d.Legacy.Update(..., objInfo, ...)` is invoked asynchronously with the original `objInfo`. That means Legacy will run `objInfo` against Legacy's own "old" state (and potentially different defaults/resourceVersion), allowing the two backends to persist different content and breaking write-equivalence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:103-107 (Delete) — early return on any storage error, including NotFound, skips the legacy delete entirely; the previous code tolerated apierrors.IsNotFound and still deleted from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy (pre-migration) can now never be cleaned up, leaving permanent orphaned legacy rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete`, the new code returns immediately on any error from `d.Storage.Delete(...)` (including a NotFound). The previous implementation explicitly tolerated `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from unified storage and still attempted `d.Legacy.Delete(...)`, allowing cleanup of objects that exist only in legacy. The new logic skips the legacy delete when storage returns NotFound, which can leave legacy-only (pre-migration) objects undeleted/orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:156-160 (DeleteCollection) — when the unified-store DeleteCollection fails, the legacy DeleteCollection is never attempted (previously it always ran), leaving orphaned legacy objects on partial failures.

adjudication.rationale:
In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DeleteCollection now returns immediately when d.Storage.DeleteCollection(...) errors:

```go
res, err := d.Storage.DeleteCollection(...)
if err != nil { ...; return res, err }
...
go func() { d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...) }()
```

Because of this early return, the legacy DeleteCollection is never attempted on unified-store failure. Previously, the legacy call was executed regardless of the storage error (it logged the storage error but continued to call d.Legacy.DeleteCollection). This is a real behavior change that can leave legacy data undeleted on partial failures, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:47 (Create) and :131 (Update) — on storage failure the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage) instead of recordStorageDuration, so storage errors are recorded as legacy-store failures and no storage-failure metric is emitted, breaking error monitoring for the primary store.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, both Create and Update record the wrong metric on primary Storage failures. In Create, after `created, err := d.Storage.Create(...)` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `recordStorageDuration(...)`, so the storage error is mis-attributed to legacy and a storage-failure duration metric is not emitted. Similarly in Update, after `res, async, err := d.Storage.Update(...)` fails, it calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage)` rather than `recordStorageDuration(...)`. This directly breaks monitoring/metrics correctness for the primary store path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:168 (DeleteCollection goroutine) — the legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded via recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency/errors to unified-storage metrics.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, the DeleteCollection method launches a goroutine to call d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...), but then records the timing via d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy) instead of a legacy-specific recorder (e.g., recordLegacyDuration). This directly misattributes legacy operation latency/error metrics to the unified storage metrics, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:52-59,110-116,136-143,163-169 — all four async legacy writes swallow errors: the result is only reflected as a boolean in a metric with no log.Error (the previous code logged legacy failures); callers get success even when the legacy write later fails, so store divergence leaves no log trail and there is no retry/reconciliation.

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy writes for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection are moved into goroutines and their returned errors are not logged anywhere (e.g., Create’s goroutine captures errObjectSt but only calls d.recordLegacyDuration(...); Delete/Update/DeleteCollection similarly). Previously, legacy failures were explicitly log.Error’d (e.g., old Create: log.WithValues(...).Error(err,...); old Update/Delete logged legacy errors). Callers still won’t see legacy failures (that was already true before), but this diff does remove the log trail and makes failures effectively silent aside from a boolean metric, which is a concrete observability/reconciliation concern rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — every Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection spawns a fire-and-forget goroutine with no queue, concurrency cap, or backpressure; under write load against a slow legacy store, thousands of concurrent legacy operations (each holding up to a 10s timeout) can pile up and exhaust the DB connection pool shared with the primary store.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Mode3 write paths to spawn unbounded fire-and-forget goroutines for legacy operations (e.g., Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection each does `go func(){ ... d.Legacy.*(...) }()` with a 10s `context.WithTimeoutCause`). There is no visible queue, concurrency limit, or backpressure mechanism in these methods, so under high write load and/or slow legacy calls, goroutines can accumulate for up to ~10s each. The finding’s specific claim about exhausting a DB connection pool shared with the primary store isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the unbounded concurrency risk introduced by the change is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — the spawned goroutines have no panic recovery; a panic inside a legacy storage implementation (or in the metric recording) on a bare goroutine crashes the entire apiserver process.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the diff introduces bare goroutines for legacy operations in Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create(...) ... }()`) without any `defer recover()` protection. In Go, an unrecovered panic in any goroutine terminates the whole process, and these goroutines are not tied to any per-request panic recovery middleware. Therefore a panic in `d.Legacy.*` or in `d.recordLegacyDuration`/`d.recordStorageDuration` inside those goroutines can crash the apiserver, a real stability defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go — async legacy writes are untracked (no WaitGroup/shutdown coordination), so writes in flight during process shutdown/restart are silently dropped with no retry, producing gaps in legacy data.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go the legacy-side operations for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection were changed from synchronous calls to fire-and-forget goroutines (e.g., `go func() { ... d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`). There is no WaitGroup, no shutdown/drain hook, and no returned error from the legacy write path; if the process exits/restarts while these goroutines are in flight, the legacy writes can be dropped, creating gaps/inconsistency in legacy data with no retry mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go — tests never assert the defining behavior of mode 3: that writes are dual-written to legacy (no assertion that LegacyStorage.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection were invoked, no AssertExpectations); because legacy writes are async, the goroutine can invoke the mock after the subtest returns (racy/flaky), and every test uses context.Background(), which is exactly why the canceled-request-context defect goes undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, legacy writes are now performed asynchronously in goroutines for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection. In the new pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go tests, mocks set up legacy expectations (e.g., m.On("Create"/"Update"/...)) but the tests never assert that legacy methods were actually invoked (no m.AssertExpectations(t) and no call count checks). Because the legacy calls happen in goroutines, the subtest can return before the legacy call occurs, making the tests potentially racy/flaky and not validating the core “dual-write to legacy” behavior. The tests also consistently use context.Background(), so they don’t exercise cancellation/timeout propagation paths introduced by the context.WithTimeoutCause usage.
